body:
- feat(convert): Attempt to come up with 256 single-token, semantic option markers

Each switch model needs to identify a collection of single-token option

markers that can be mapped to their respective logits for the output

probability distribution. The simple upper/lower/numbers set only yields 66

unique markers, but the model can support up to 255. The challenge is that

which combinations of characters result in single-token markers is model-

specific, so we do a discovery exercise at conversion time by looking

through the specific model's vocab for single-token sequences of 1+ plain

letter strings (eg A , AA , BB , etc).

Branch: GraniteSwitchDecisionFullOptions

Signed-off-by: Gabe Goodhart ghart@us.ibm.com

- docs: Note granite-switch with 256 option markers

- style: Remove extra newline
